title: DFMEA Risk Priority Number Calculation
problem: Automotive engineers must calculate Risk Priority Numbers (RPNs) for every potential failure mode in DFMEA documents, multiplying severity, occurrence, and detection ratings across dozens or hundreds of components. Manual calculation in spreadsheets is error-prone and time-consuming, and incorrect RPNs can lead to missed safety-critical failures that result in recalls.
who: Mid-level and senior design engineers responsible for DFMEA documentation

skill_spec.name: DFMEA RPN Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates Risk Priority Numbers and Action Priority rankings for DFMEA failure modes per SAE J1739/AIAG-VDA methodology

inputs.name: method
inputs.label: Method: classic RPN or AIAG-VDA Action Priority

skill_spec.formula_hint: Classic: RPN = S * O * D. AIAG-VDA: use severity-occurrence-detection lookup table for Action Priority (H/M/L). Flag RPN > 100 or severity >= 9 as critical.

example_queries: Calculate RPN for a brake caliper seal failure with severity 9, occurrence 4, detection 6
I have 5 failure modes for a steering column - rate them using AIAG-VDA action priority method
Is an RPN of 120 on a fuel line connector considered critical?

title: BOM Cost Estimation and Rollup
problem: Engineers frequently need to estimate component and assembly costs for Bill of Materials during design reviews, RFQ responses, and cost reduction initiatives. Manually rolling up costs across multi-level BOMs with hundreds of parts, factoring in material costs, tooling amortization, and supplier markups is tedious and often inaccurate, leading to budget overruns.
who: Design engineers and cost estimators preparing for PDR/CDR reviews

skill_spec.name: BOM Cost Rollup Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates total assembly cost from component costs, tooling amortization, labor, and supplier markup across BOM levels

inputs.name: components
inputs.label: List of components with unit costs

skill_spec.formula_hint: Piece cost = sum(component_costs * qty). Tooling/unit = tooling_cost / (annual_volume * life_years). Labor/unit = (assembly_time/60) * labor_rate. Total = (piece + tooling + labor) * (1 + markup%)

example_queries: Estimate unit cost for a bracket assembly: 3 stamped parts at $2.50 each, $180K tooling over 5 years, 100K annual volume
What's the cost per unit if tooling is $500K amortized over 3 years at 200K units per year with 12% supplier markup?
Roll up BOM cost for a door module with 15 components totaling $47 in piece cost plus $8 labor

title: Engineering Change Notice (ECN) Process
problem: Engineering Change Notices require coordinating across design, manufacturing, quality, purchasing, and supplier teams. Missing a step - like failing to update the BOM, notify affected suppliers, or get proper sign-offs - can delay production, create inventory waste, or introduce quality defects. Engineers spend hours tracking the status of ECNs across departments.
who: All automotive engineers initiating or impacted by design changes

skill_spec.name: ECN Processing Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step Engineering Change Notice workflow ensuring all stakeholders, documents, and systems are updated
steps: Step 1: Document change request with rationale (cost, quality, safety, regulation)
Step 2: Perform impact analysis - affected parts, assemblies, tooling, and suppliers
Step 3: Update CAD models and engineering drawings with new revision level
Step 4: Update BOM in PLM system (Teamcenter/Windchill/3DEXPERIENCE)
Step 5: Run DFMEA update for affected failure modes
Step 6: Obtain cross-functional sign-offs (Design, Manufacturing, Quality, Purchasing)
Step 7: Notify affected suppliers with updated specs and timeline
Step 8: Determine effectivity date and inventory disposition plan
Step 9: Update test/validation plan if design intent changed
Step 10: Release ECN in PLM and distribute to all stakeholders
Step 11: Verify PPAP re-submission requirements with suppliers
Step 12: Archive superseded documentation
warnings: Warning: Safety-critical changes (FMVSS-related) require additional regulatory review before release
Warning: Changes after design freeze require program director approval
Warning: Supplier tooling changes may require new PPAP submission per AIAG guidelines

example_queries: I need to change a brake rotor material from cast iron to carbon ceramic - what's the full ECN process?
What approvals do I need for an ECN after design freeze?
Checklist for processing an engineering change on a safety-critical suspension component

title: FMVSS Compliance Requirements Lookup
problem: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards span hundreds of regulations across crashworthiness, crash avoidance, and post-crash survivability. Engineers waste significant time searching through NHTSA documents to find which FMVSS applies to their component, what the specific test requirements are, and what the pass/fail criteria are. Misinterpreting a standard can lead to costly test failures or non-compliance.
who: Design and validation engineers working on safety-relevant components

skill_spec.name: FMVSS Quick Reference Guide
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards by component, system, or vehicle type with test requirements and pass/fail criteria
skill_spec.data_domain: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (49 CFR Part 571) - all active FMVSS numbers, applicable vehicle categories, test procedures, and performance requirements

data_hints.source_law: 49 CFR Part 571 - Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards

example_queries: Which FMVSS standards apply to a new EV battery enclosure?
What are the FMVSS 208 frontal crash test requirements for passenger cars?
What's the minimum performance requirement for FMVSS 135 brake systems?

title: Tolerance Stack-Up Analysis
problem: Engineers must calculate worst-case and statistical tolerance stack-ups for assemblies to ensure parts fit and function correctly. Manual stack-up calculations across 10-20 contributing dimensions are tedious, error-prone, and critical - a wrong tolerance can mean parts don't assemble on the production line, causing line stoppages costing $10K+ per minute.
who: Design engineers and dimensional engineers working on multi-part assemblies

skill_spec.name: Tolerance Stack-Up Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Performs worst-case and RSS (Root Sum Square) statistical tolerance stack-up analysis for linear dimension chains

inputs.name: dimensions
inputs.label: List of nominal dimensions with +/- tolerances

inputs.name: direction
inputs.label: Direction for each dimension (positive/negative in chain)

inputs.name: method
inputs.label: Analysis method: Worst-Case or RSS Statistical

skill_spec.formula_hint: Worst-case: total_tol = sum(all tolerances). RSS: total_tol = sqrt(sum(tol_i^2)). Cpk = min((USL-mean)/(3*sigma), (mean-LSL)/(3*sigma)). Gap = nominal_sum(positive) - nominal_sum(negative).

example_queries: Stack-up analysis for 5 parts in a door hinge assembly: 10mm +/-0.1, 25mm +/-0.2, 8mm +/-0.05, 15mm +/-0.15, 12mm +/-0.1
Will a 0.5mm minimum gap requirement pass with RSS method at 3-sigma for these 8 contributing tolerances?
Calculate Cpk for a stack-up with nominal gap 1.2mm and RSS tolerance of 0.45mm

title: PPAP Submission Preparation
problem: Production Part Approval Process requires assembling 18 specific elements (design records, process flow diagrams, measurement system analysis, etc.) in the correct format for customer submission. Engineers and quality teams frequently miss elements or submit incorrect levels, causing rejections that delay SoP and strain supplier relationships.
who: Quality engineers and design engineers at Tier 1/Tier 2 suppliers

skill_spec.name: PPAP Submission Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Complete checklist for PPAP submission levels 1-5 per AIAG PPAP Manual 4th Edition with all 18 required elements
steps: Step 1: Confirm PPAP submission level (1-5) required by customer
Step 2: Prepare design records (drawings with ballooned dimensions)
Step 3: Document authorized engineering changes
Step 4: Obtain customer engineering approval (if required)
Step 5: Create DFMEA document
Step 6: Create process flow diagram
Step 7: Create PFMEA (Process FMEA)
Step 8: Create control plan
Step 9: Perform Measurement System Analysis (MSA/GR&R)
Step 10: Collect dimensional results (minimum 30 parts for initial study)
Step 11: Document material and performance test results
Step 12: Perform initial process study (Cpk/Ppk calculations)
Step 13: Complete qualified laboratory documentation
Step 14: Prepare Appearance Approval Report (AAR) if applicable
Step 15: Collect sample production parts
Step 16: Prepare master sample
Step 17: Document checking aids
Step 18: Document customer-specific requirements
Step 19: Complete Part Submission Warrant (PSW) and obtain signatures
Step 20: Submit package and track customer disposition
warnings: Warning: Level 3 (default) requires all 18 elements submitted to customer
Warning: Cpk < 1.33 requires corrective action plan before submission
Warning: Safety/regulatory characteristics (CC/SC) require 100% inspection documentation

example_queries: What documents do I need for a PPAP Level 3 submission?
Our Cpk came in at 1.1 on a critical dimension - can we still submit PPAP?
Checklist for PPAP resubmission after an engineering change on a stamped bracket

title: EPA Emissions Compliance Standards Lookup
problem: With rapidly changing EPA emissions regulations (Tier 3, LEV IV, and new EV-related standards), engineers struggle to find current emission limits, test procedures, and phase-in schedules for their specific vehicle class and model year. Non-compliance can result in massive fines, production halts, and mandatory recalls.
who: Powertrain engineers and emissions calibration engineers

skill_spec.name: EPA Emissions Standards Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of EPA Tier 3/LEV IV emission limits, test procedures, and phase-in schedules by vehicle class and model year
skill_spec.data_domain: EPA Light-Duty Vehicle Emissions Standards (40 CFR Part 86), Tier 3 and greenhouse gas regulations, CARB LEV IV standards

data_hints.source_law: Clean Air Act, 40 CFR Parts 86 and 1066
carb_standards: LEV IV (Super Ultra Low Emission Vehicle)

example_queries: What are the Tier 3 Bin 70 emission limits for a 2026 model year light-duty truck?
What's the EPA fleet average NMOG+NOx target for MY2026?
What are CARB LEV IV SULEV30 standards for a passenger car?

title: FEA Simulation Results Validation Report
problem: After running FEA or CFD simulations, engineers must document results in a standardized report format for design reviews (PDR/CDR). Writing these reports from scratch is time-consuming and inconsistent across teams. Missing key sections (boundary conditions, mesh convergence, safety factors) leads to review rejections and rework.
who: CAE analysts and design engineers presenting at PDR/CDR reviews

skill_spec.name: FEA/CFD Simulation Report Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates a standardized simulation report for design reviews including all required sections for PDR/CDR presentation

variables.name: analysis_type
variables.label: Analysis type (Static FEA, Modal, Thermal, CFD, Fatigue)

variables.name: mesh_details
variables.label: Mesh type, element count, quality metrics

variables.name: results_summary
variables.label: Key results (max stress, displacement, safety factor)

variables.name: pass_fail_criteria
variables.label: Acceptance criteria and margin of safety

skill_spec.structure_hint: Executive Summary -> Objective -> Model Description (geometry, material, mesh) -> Boundary Conditions & Load Cases -> Results (contour plots description, max values, locations) -> Convergence Study -> Safety Factor Analysis -> Conclusions & Recommendations -> Appendix (detailed data)

example_queries: Generate a simulation report for static FEA of a control arm under 3G braking load
I need a PDR-ready report template for thermal analysis of a battery enclosure
Create a CFD report for underhood airflow analysis on a new front-end design

title: Bolt Torque and Joint Calculation
problem: Automotive engineers constantly calculate bolt torque specifications, clamping force, and joint integrity for threaded fastener connections. Wrong torque specs can lead to joint failure, loosening under vibration, or bolt fracture - all safety-critical in automotive applications. Engineers reference VDI 2230 guidelines and perform manual calculations that are prone to unit conversion errors.
who: Design engineers working on structural and chassis components

skill_spec.name: Bolt Torque & Clamping Force Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates target torque, clamping force, and bolt stress for threaded fastener joints per VDI 2230 methodology
skill_spec.formula_hint: T = F_clamp * d * (0.16*p + 0.58*d2*mu_th + D_bearing/2*mu_uh). Bolt stress = F/(A_stress). SF_yield = Rp0.2*A_stress/F_bolt_max. SF_separation = F_clamp_residual/F_external. Use VDI 2230 systematic approach.

example_queries: What torque for an M10x1.5 grade 10.9 bolt with 0.14 friction coefficient and 25kN required clamping force?
Calculate if an M8 class 8.8 bolt can handle 12kN external load with adequate safety factor
Torque spec for M6x1.0 grade 12.9 in a tapped aluminum housing

title: ISO 26262 Functional Safety ASIL Determination
problem: Engineers developing safety-critical automotive systems must determine the Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) for each hazard per ISO 26262. The ASIL classification involves evaluating severity, exposure probability, and controllability for each operational scenario - a structured but complex process where errors can lead to under-engineering safety measures or over-engineering costs.
who: Systems engineers and functional safety engineers working on ADAS, braking, steering, or EV systems

skill_spec.name: ISO 26262 ASIL Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Determines ASIL classification (A/B/C/D/QM) from severity, exposure, and controllability ratings per ISO 26262 Part 3

inputs.name: exposure
inputs.label: Exposure probability (E0-E4: incredible to high probability)

outputs.name: asil_level
outputs.label: ASIL classification (QM, A, B, C, or D)

outputs.name: safety_requirements
outputs.label: Summary of required safety measures for this ASIL

skill_spec.formula_hint: ASIL lookup table: S3+E4+C3=ASIL D, S3+E4+C2=ASIL C, etc. QM = no automotive safety requirement. ASIL D is most stringent. Decomposition: ASIL D can split into ASIL C(D) + ASIL A(D) on redundant paths.

example_queries: Determine ASIL for unintended acceleration at highway speed: severity S3, exposure E4, controllability C2
What ASIL level if severity is S2, exposure E3, controllability C3?
Can I decompose an ASIL D requirement for a redundant braking system?

title: 8D Problem-Solving Report
problem: When quality issues arise in production or from customer complaints, engineers must complete 8D (Eight Disciplines) problem-solving reports. These reports require a structured methodology that many engineers struggle with - particularly defining the root cause analysis, containment actions, and verification steps. Incomplete or poorly written 8Ds get rejected by OEM customers.
who: Quality engineers and design engineers at suppliers responding to customer complaints

skill_spec.name: 8D Report Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates a structured 8D problem-solving report with all eight disciplines properly documented for OEM customer submission

variables.name: problem_description
variables.label: Problem description (what, where, when, how many)

skill_spec.structure_hint: D0: Awareness/Emergency Response -> D1: Team Formation -> D2: Problem Description (IS/IS NOT) -> D3: Interim Containment Actions -> D4: Root Cause Analysis (5-Why, Fishbone) -> D5: Permanent Corrective Actions -> D6: Implementation & Validation -> D7: Preventive Actions (systemic) -> D8: Team Recognition & Close-out

example_queries: Generate an 8D report for a cracked weld on a suspension crossmember found at customer assembly plant
Help me write D4 root cause analysis for a dimensional issue on stamped brackets using 5-Why method
Create 8D template for a paint adhesion failure on exterior trim parts

title: EV Transition Career and Skills Advisor
problem: With the rapid shift to electric vehicles, many ICE-focused automotive engineers fear obsolescence. They need guidance on which skills to develop (battery systems, power electronics, BMS, thermal management), which certifications matter, and how to position their existing experience for EV roles. The transition path is unclear and anxiety-inducing.
who: Mid-career powertrain and mechanical engineers (5-15 years experience) in traditional ICE roles

skill_spec.name: EV Transition Career Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Provides personalized guidance for ICE automotive engineers transitioning to EV roles including skills mapping, certifications, and career positioning
skill_spec.expertise_area: Automotive engineering career transition from ICE to EV/electrification

example_queries: I'm a 10-year ICE powertrain calibration engineer - what EV skills should I develop first?
Which certifications are worth getting for battery systems engineering?
How do I position my NVH experience for an EV role at Rivian or Tesla?

title: Material Selection and Properties Reference
problem: Engineers frequently need to look up material properties (yield strength, fatigue limit, thermal conductivity, density) for automotive-grade steels, aluminum alloys, polymers, and composites during design and simulation work. Searching through material datasheets and standards is slow, and using wrong properties in FEA leads to invalid simulation results.
who: Design engineers and CAE analysts selecting materials for components

skill_spec.name: Automotive Materials Properties Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of mechanical, thermal, and fatigue properties for common automotive-grade materials (steels, aluminum, polymers, composites)
skill_spec.data_domain: Automotive engineering materials: AHSS, HSLA steels, aluminum 5xxx/6xxx/7xxx series, engineering polymers (PA6, PA66-GF, PBT, PP), CFRP, magnesium alloys

example_queries: What are the mechanical properties of DP780 dual-phase steel?
Compare yield strength and density of AA6061-T6 vs DP590 for a lightweighting study
What's the fatigue limit of SAE 4140 QT steel for a suspension component?
